title: The guard's orphan self-heal retires a FRESH pipeline's sentinel: in a repo with no linked worktree, the first base-clone command disarms the guard for the whole session
body:
## Summary

`fr-isolation-guard.sh`'s orphan self-heal (#341 Task 2A) cannot tell a sentinel that has **outlived** its worktrees from one that **has not created one yet**. In a repo with no linked worktree, the first base-clone command of a brand-new pipeline — any command, `ls` included — deletes that pipeline's sentinel and exits 0. The bash guard is then inert for the rest of the session, and nothing says so.

This is the mirror image of #472 (the heal *fails* to fire when other sessions have worktrees). Same predicate, opposite failure — and **it constrains #472's fix**, see below.

Found while root-causing C4 in #527 (`docs/superpowers/journals/debug/2026-09-21-508-live-test-plan-defects.md`, entry `c4-root-cause`). It is *why* C4 hid: my first repro of "the guard denies `fr run start`" came back all-allow, because the heal had quietly removed the sentinel first.

## Repro

Using the hook's own test harness (`tests/unit/test_hooks_guard.py`: `write_sentinel`, `payload`, `run_hook`, `decision`):

1. `git init` a repo — **no** linked worktrees. Write a sentinel for session `s` with that `repo_root` (what `fr-pipeline-sentinel.sh` does when a pipeline skill loads).
2. Run the guard for **any** command with `cwd` in the repo.

Observed: `allow`, and `sentinels/s.json` is gone. Every later command in that session is ungated.

3. Add one linked worktree on any branch (anyone's) and repeat with a fresh sentinel: `deny`, sentinel kept — the intended behaviour.

So whether a new pipeline is guarded depends on whether the repo *happens* to already have someone's worktree.

## Mechanism

`hooks/fr-isolation-guard.sh`, the self-heal block:

```bash
if wt=$(git -C "$rroot" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null); then
  n=$(printf '%s\n' "$wt" | grep -c '^worktree ' || true)
  if [ "${n:-0}" -eq 1 ]; then
    rm -f "$sentinel" || true
    exit 0
  fi
fi
```

"Exactly one `worktree` line" is read as *the sentinel outlived all worktrees*. At pipeline start it is equally true, for the opposite reason: the pipeline's first action (`fr run start` / `fr isolation up`) has not run yet.

Ordering makes it worse. The sentinel is written when the skill **loads**; the workspace is created by the skill's first **command**. Anything the agent runs in between — and agents do run a `git status` or an `ls` first, despite the skill saying not to — takes the heal path.

## Why this matters more than it looks

It fails **open**, silently, on exactly the sessions the guard exists for: a first pipeline in a repo. Once `fr run start` has created the worktree, the repo has two `worktree` lines and the guard *would* work — but the sentinel is already gone, so it never gets the chance.

## Constraint on #472

#472's suggested fix 1 is: *"Fail open and clear the sentinel when **this session** has no live workspace, rather than when the repo has none."* A freshly started pipeline is precisely a session with no live workspace. Implemented as written, that turns this defect from "only in worktree-less repos" into "every repo, every pipeline". Whatever replaces the repo-wide count has to distinguish **never had one** from **had one, lost it**.

## Shape of a fix (not a recommendation)

Make "has this pipeline ever had a workspace" a recorded fact rather than an inference:

- stamp the sentinel when a workspace is first bound to it (`fr isolation up` / `fr run start` already know the session), and heal only a sentinel that carries the stamp and whose workspace is gone; or
- give a fresh sentinel a grace window before it is eligible for healing — cheaper, but it is a timeout standing in for a fact.

The first fails at the right place: a sentinel with no stamp is *new*, a sentinel with a stamp and no workspace is *orphaned*, and neither is guessed from `git worktree list`.

## Related

- **#472 (open)** — same predicate, opposite failure; see the constraint above.
- **#432 (open)** — what the denial says once the worktree is gone.
- **#341 / #344 / #329** — shipped the heal this is about.
- **#527** — C4, where this was found; `TestRunStartEntersIsolation` there deliberately uses a non-git dir (the heal fails closed) so its assertions are about the allowlist alone.
